Section(s): 2.1. Biomass growth; 2.6. Penicillin production; 2.7. Substrate utilization

Text and equations in reading order:
    Experimental findings suggest a high degree of dependence of biomass growth on both the carbon source (glucose) and oxygen as substrates (Bajpai & Reuss, 1980). The biomass growth is also known to be inhibited by high amounts of biomass itself in penicillin fermentation. The dependence of specific growth rate on carbon and oxygen substrates was assumed to follow Contois kinetics (Bajpai & Reuss) to consider the biomass inhibition. The biomass growth has been described as:
(1) \frac{\mathrm{d}X}{\mathrm{d}t}=\mu X-\frac{X}{V}\frac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t}    [code: ODE, computes X, code proposes balance]
    where the specific growth rate $ \mu $ was:
    in the original model (Bajpai & Reuss, 1980). The variables and parameters used are defined in Tables 1 and 2. Environmental variables such as pH and temperature play an important role on the quality and quantity of the final product. In order to take these effects into account, biomass formation has been related to these variables by introducing their effects in the specific growth rate expression to give:
(3) \begin{aligned}\mu&=\left[\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{x}}}{1+{[K_{1}/[\mathrm{H}^{+}]]}+[[[\mathrm{H}^{+}]]/K_{2}]}\right]\frac{S}{K_{\mathrm{x}}X+S}\\&\quad\times\frac{C_{\mathrm{L}}}{K_{\mathrm{ox}}X+C_{\mathrm{L}}}\\&\left[k_{\mathrm{g}}\exp\left(-\frac{E_{\mathrm{g}}}{\mathrm{RT}}\right)\right]-\left[k_{\mathrm{d}}\exp\left(-\frac{E_{\mathrm{d}}}{\mathrm{RT}}\right)\right].\end{aligned}    [code: algebraic, computes \mu, code proposes constitutive]
    This would in turn affect the utilization of substrate and the production of penicillin. Direct effects of pH and temperature on penicillin production are not considered due to the complex nature of the phenomenon, and unavailability of the experimental data.
    The production of penicillin is described by non-growth associated product formation kinetics. The hydrolysis of penicillin is also included in the rate expression (Bajpai & Reuss, 1980):
(9) \frac{\mathrm{d}P}{\mathrm{d}t}=\mu_{\mathrm{pp}}X-KP-\frac{P}{V}\frac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t}    [code: ODE, computes P, code proposes balance]
    where, $ \mu_{pp} $ is the specific penicillin production rate defined as:
(10) \mu_{\mathrm{pp}}=\mu_{\mathrm{p}}\frac{S}{(K_{\mathrm{p}}+S+S^{2}/K_{\mathrm{I}})}\frac{C^{\mathrm{p}}_{\mathrm{L}}}{(K_{\mathrm{op}}X+C^{\mathrm{p}}_{\mathrm{L}})}    [code: algebraic, computes \mu_{pp}, code proposes constitutive]
    Substrate inhibition kinetics for penicillin production was originally proposed by Bajpai and Reuss (1980) that successfully represented the observed behavior. They commented that the proposed mechanism should not be considered to throw any light upon the nature of phenomena involved. Others point out that industrial strains of penicillin production are tolerant to high levels of glucose and question the use of substrate inhibition terms in Eq. (10). Large quantities of substrate results in only little improvement of penicillin production.
    Glucose:
(11) \frac{\mathrm{d}S}{\mathrm{d}t}=-\frac{\mu}{Y_{\mathrm{x/s}}}X-\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{pp}}}{Y_{\mathrm{p/s}}}X-m_{\mathrm{x}}X+\frac{Fs_{\mathrm{f}}}{V}-\frac{S}{V}\frac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t}    [code: ODE, computes S, code proposes balance]
    Dissolved oxygen:
(12) \begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}C_{\mathrm{L}}}{\mathrm{d}t}=&-\frac{\mu}{Y_{\mathrm{x/o}}}\ X-\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{pp}}}{Y_{\mathrm{p/o}}}\ X-m_{\mathrm{o}}X+K_{\mathrm{la}}(C_{\mathrm{L}}^{*}-C_{\mathrm{L}})-\frac{C_{\mathrm{L}}}{V}\\&\times\frac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t}\tag{12}\end{aligned}    [code: ODE, computes C_{L}, code proposes balance]
    In the original model of Bajpai and Reuss, the overall mass transfer coefficient $ K_{la} $ is constant (Bajpai & Reuss, 1980). Here we have assumed $ K_{la} $ to be a function of agitation power input $ P_{w} $ and flow rate of oxygen $ f_{g} $ as suggested by Bailey and Ollis (1986).
(13) K_{\mathrm{l a}}=\alpha\sqrt{f_{\mathrm{g}}}\biggl(\frac{P_{\mathrm{w}}}{V}\biggr)^{\beta}    [code: algebraic, computes K_{la}, code proposes constitutive]
    The values of $ \alpha $ and $ \beta $ are assigned so that the dependence of penicillin concentration on $ K_{la} $ showed a very similar behavior to the predictions of Bajpai and Reuss (1980). This has been discussed in detail in Section 4.

Symbols:
  X: Biomass concentration [g/l] (computed)
  \mu: Specific growth rate [h^-1] (computed)
  V: Culture volume [l] (computed)
  \mu_{x}: Maximum specific growth rate [per h] (parameter)
  K_{1}: Hydrogen-ion inhibition constant in the specific growth-rate expression [mol/l] (parameter)
  [H^+]: Hydrogen ion concentration [mol/l] (variable)
  K_{2}: Hydrogen-ion inhibition constant in the specific growth-rate expression [mol/l] (parameter)
  S: Substrate concentration [g/l] (computed)
  K_{x}: Contois saturation constant [g/l] (parameter)
  C_{L}: Dissolved oxygen concentration [g/l] (computed)
  K_{ox}: Oxygen limitation constant (parameter)
  k_{g}: Arrhenius constant for growth [h^-1] (parameter)
  E_{g}: Activation energy for growth [cal/mol] (parameter)
  R: Universal gas constant in the Arrhenius expression [cal mol^-1 K^-1] (parameter)
  T: Temperature [K] (computed)
  k_{d}: Arrhenius constant for cell death [h^-1] (parameter)
  E_{d}: Activation energy for cell death [cal/mol] (parameter)
  P: Penicillin concentration [g/l] (computed)
  \mu_{pp}: Specific penicillin production rate [h^-1] (computed)
  K: Penicillin hydrolysis rate constant [per h] (parameter)
  \mu_{p}: Specific rate of penicillin production [per h] (parameter)
  K_{p}: Inhibition constant [g/l] (parameter)
  K_{I}: Substrate inhibition constant in the S²/K_I term [g/l] (parameter)
  p: Constant, used as the exponent in the oxygen-limitation term [-] (parameter)
  K_{op}: Oxygen limitation constant [-] (parameter)
  Y_{x/s}: Yield constant for biomass on glucose [g biomass/g glucose] (parameter)
  Y_{p/s}: Yield constant for penicillin on glucose [g penicillin/g glucose] (parameter)
  m_{x}: Maintenance coefficient on substrate [per h] (parameter)
  F: Feed flow rate of substrate [l/h] (variable)
  s_{f}: Feed substrate concentration [g/l] (variable)
  Y_{x/o}: Yield constant for biomass per oxygen [g biomass/g oxygen] (parameter)
  Y_{p/o}: Yield constant for penicillin per oxygen [g penicillin/g oxygen] (parameter)
  m_{o}: Maintenance coefficient on oxygen [per h] (parameter)
  K_{la}: Overall mass transfer coefficient [h^-1] (computed)
  C_{L}^{*}: Dissolved oxygen concentration at saturation [g/l] (parameter)
  \alpha: Constant in the K_la correlation (parameter)
  f_{g}: Flow rate of oxygen (variable)
  P_{w}: Agitation power input (variable)
  \beta: Constant in the K_la correlation [-] (parameter)
